g.text: The same core, at the same coordinates, three times; lost edges stay in orange. And the result inverts here: removing finance takes 652 of the core's 1,388 edges, against 666 for the same number of firms drawn at

random from within the core itself. That is expected and worth seeing: the core is the 170 firms of highest weighted degree, so a random draw inside it is a draw of hubs. The core cannot separate sectors. On the

whole graph, where the draw is genuinely arbitrary, finance does separate: z = +3.35 against z = -0.11 for mining, at 533 and 530 firms; and the cost reads as distance, the mean path lengthening by +0.2956 against
+0.0896. No sector fragments the network — the giant component stays at 98.6%.
